questions.question: Majuli, in the Brahmaputra River, holds which world record?
Majuli is a major centre of which religious-cultural institution unique to Assam?
Majuli faces significant erosion from which river?
Majuli's sattras were founded in the 15th-16th century by which saint-reformer?
What has Majuli lost roughly two-thirds of since the early 20th century due to erosion?

pins.summary: Majuli in the Brahmaputra is the world's largest river island, though relentless erosion has shrunk it from roughly 1,250 sq km a century ago to under 500 sq km today. It is the spiritual heart of Assam's Vaishnavite tradition, home to sattras — monastery-cum-cultural-centres founded by the 15th-16th century reformer Srimanta Sankardeva — that still teach classical mask-making, dance, and manuscript painting. Majuli's mostly tribal and Mishing population lives on stilted bamboo houses adapted to seasonal flooding, and the island was in serious contention to be declared India's first island district.

questions.question: The Great Rann of Kutch is best described as which type of terrain?
The Rann Utsav festival is held annually near which town in Kutch?
During the monsoon, the Great Rann largely becomes what?
The Great Rann of Kutch borders which country?
The Rann is home to which unique wildlife sanctuary for a large mammal?

pins.summary: The Great Rann of Kutch is one of the world's largest salt marshes, a roughly 7,500 sq km expanse that floods during the monsoon and dries into a blinding white salt desert by winter. Every winter the Gujarat government's Rann Utsav transforms the village of Dhordo into a tented festival city celebrating Kutchi music, crafts, and cuisine under full-moon nights. The Rann also hosts the Indian Wild Ass Sanctuary, protecting the last wild population of the native khur, and its stark whiteness is visible even from space.

questions.question: Barren Island is notable in India for being its only what?
Barren Island lies in which body of water?
In which decade did Barren Island's volcano have a major eruption after roughly 150 years of dormancy?
Barren Island is administratively part of which Union Territory?
Is Barren Island permanently inhabited by people?

pins.summary: Barren Island, roughly 140 km northeast of Port Blair, is India's only confirmed active volcano and one of very few in all of South Asia. Dormant for about a century and a half, it reawakened in 1991 and has erupted intermittently since, most notably during the 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake period. The island is uninhabited and largely barren, as its name suggests, with a stark black cone rising from turquoise water — visited mainly by researchers and the occasional adventure diving expedition, since landing is heavily restricted.

questions.question: Dzükou Valley is popularly nicknamed after which flower it is famous for?
options: Valley of Flowers of the Northeast

questions.question: Dzükou Valley sits on the border between Nagaland and which other state?
The valley is accessible primarily via trekking from which Nagaland town?
In 2020, Dzükou Valley suffered significant damage from what natural event?
The valley is especially famous for its blooms of which specific lily species?

pins.summary: Dzükou Valley, straddling the Nagaland-Manipur border near Kohima, is one of Northeast India's most celebrated trekking destinations — a high-altitude valley that turns carpet-green in monsoon and bursts with seasonal blooms, including the rare Dzükou lily found almost nowhere else. The valley has no road access; reaching it requires a steep trek of several hours, which has helped preserve its untouched character. In December 2020, a large wildfire — reportedly started by trekkers' campfires — burned through a significant portion of the valley, prompting stricter access controls.

questions.question: Loktak Lake is famous for its floating masses of vegetation called what?
Loktak Lake is the largest freshwater lake in which part of India?
Keibul Lamjao, the world's only floating national park, sits within Loktak Lake to protect which endangered deer?
Loktak Lake is a vital source of livelihood for local fisherfolk who build floating huts called what?
Loktak Lake was designated a Ramsar Wetland of International Importance in which year?

pins.summary: Loktak Lake in Manipur is the largest freshwater lake in Northeast India, famous for its phumdis — thick floating mats of vegetation and soil that drift across the water and are even used to build fishing huts called athaphums. At its heart sits Keibul Lamjao, the world's only floating national park, created specifically to protect the sangai, Manipur's endangered brow-antlered deer, which lives on the springy phumdi terrain found nowhere else on Earth. Loktak has been a Ramsar-listed wetland since 1990, though it faces ongoing environmental pressure from a hydroelectric project and pollution.

questions.question: The Great Stupa at Sanchi was originally commissioned by which emperor?
Sanchi's stupas primarily commemorate the life and relics of which figure?
The four ornately carved gateways at the Great Stupa are called what?
In which century BCE was the core of the Great Stupa originally built?
Sanchi was rediscovered and later restored in the 19th century after being found in what state?

pins.summary: The Great Stupa at Sanchi, originally commissioned by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE, is among the oldest surviving stone structures in India. Its four intricately carved toranas (gateways), added later by the Satavahanas, depict scenes from the Buddha's life and Jataka tales in a style that predates figurative depictions of the Buddha himself — he appears only through symbols like the wheel and the empty throne. Abandoned and left to decay for centuries after Buddhism's decline in India, Sanchi was rediscovered in 1818 and carefully restored, earning UNESCO World Heritage status in 1989.

questions.question: Rani ki Vav is an elaborate example of which type of traditional water structure?
Rani ki Vav was built in memory of which Solanki dynasty king by his widowed queen?
Rani ki Vav appeared on which Indian currency note starting 2018?
The stepwell was buried under silt from a nearby river for centuries before excavation. Which river caused this?
Rani ki Vav was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in which year?

pins.summary: Rani ki Vav in Patan, Gujarat, is widely regarded as India's finest surviving stepwell — an inverted temple of sculpted galleries descending seven levels underground, built around 1063 CE by Queen Udayamati in memory of her husband, King Bhimdev I of the Solanki dynasty. Buried under silt from the Saraswati River for centuries, it was excavated only in the 1980s, which paradoxically preserved its more than 1,500 sculptural panels in remarkable condition. Since 2018, its image has appeared on the reverse of the Indian ₹100 note, and UNESCO listed it as a World Heritage Site in 2014.

questions.question: The Elephanta Caves are rock-cut temples primarily dedicated to which deity?
Elephanta Island lies in which body of water near Mumbai?
The caves' most famous sculpture is a three-faced bust representing Shiva known as what?
The island's name 'Elephanta' was given by which colonial power, after a stone elephant statue they found there?
The Elephanta Caves are estimated to have been carved primarily in which century CE?

pins.summary: The Elephanta Caves, on an island in Mumbai Harbour reachable by a short ferry ride, are a network of rock-cut temples carved mainly in the 5th-6th centuries CE, dedicated overwhelmingly to Shiva. Their centerpiece is the towering Sadashiva or Trimurti sculpture — a six-metre bust with three faces representing creation, preservation, and destruction — considered one of the masterpieces of Indian rock-cut art. The Portuguese named the island after a large stone elephant statue they found near the shore (now relocated to a Mumbai museum), and the caves have been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987.

questions.question: Mehrangarh Fort overlooks which Rajasthani city, known as the Blue City?
Mehrangarh Fort was founded in which century by Rao Jodha?
The fort sits atop a hill rising how high above the surrounding city?
Mehrangarh's massive walls are, in places, how thick?
The fort houses a museum showcasing collections of what, among other things?

pins.summary: Mehrangarh Fort rises dramatically some 125 metres above Jodhpur — the Blue City — its walls in places up to 36 metres high and 21 metres thick, founded in 1459 by Rao Jodha, the Rathore ruler who established the city itself. One of India's most formidable and best-preserved forts, it was never conquered despite centuries of regional conflict. Today it houses a well-curated museum of royal palanquins, weaponry, textiles, and Rajput miniature paintings, and its ramparts offer sweeping views over Jodhpur's famous blue-painted old town below.

questions.question: The Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram was built by which dynasty?
The Shore Temple sits directly beside which body of water?
The temple complex is primarily dedicated to which two deities?
Mahabalipuram's monuments, including the Shore Temple, were built mainly during the reign of which Pallava king?
The 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami briefly exposed what near the Shore Temple, fueling theories of a submerged ancient city?
options: Additional stone structures on the seabed

pins.summary: The Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram, built by the Pallava dynasty in the early 8th century, is one of the oldest surviving structural stone temples in South India, standing directly on the Bay of Bengal shoreline where centuries of salt spray have worn its granite surfaces smooth. Dedicated jointly to Shiva and Vishnu, it forms part of a larger complex of rock-cut monuments developed under King Narasimhavarman I. After the devastating 2004 tsunami briefly receded the sea, additional stone structures were glimpsed on the seabed nearby, reviving long-standing legends of a larger submerged temple city — the fabled 'Seven Pagodas' of Mahabalipuram.

questions.question: The Jamnagar Refinery, operated by Reliance Industries, is recognised as the world's what?
Jamnagar Refinery is located in which Indian state?
The Jamnagar complex actually consists of how many separate refineries built side by side?
Jamnagar Refinery's combined processing capacity handles roughly how many barrels of crude oil per day?
Reliance's second refinery unit at Jamnagar, completed in 2008, was built primarily to focus on what?

pins.summary: The Jamnagar Refinery Complex in Gujarat, operated by Reliance Industries, is the world's largest single-location oil refining complex, combining two refineries with a joint capacity of about 1.24 million barrels per day. The original refinery opened in 1999; a second, export-oriented unit was added in 2008, doubling capacity and making Jamnagar a critical hub feeding fuel to markets across Asia, Europe, and beyond. The complex sprawls across roughly 7,500 acres and functions almost like a self-contained industrial township, complete with its own port and power plant.

questions.question: Visakhapatnam Port is one of India's deepest natural ports on which coast?
Visakhapatnam Port primarily handles bulk exports of which commodity historically?
Visakhapatnam is also home to a major base for which branch of the Indian armed forces?
Visakhapatnam Port was established under British administration in which decade?
Which Andhra Pradesh city, home to this port, is nicknamed 'The City of Destiny'?

pins.summary: Visakhapatnam Port on India's east coast is among the country's deepest natural harbours, historically built around bulk exports of iron ore, coal, and manganese from the mineral-rich interior of Odisha and Chhattisgarh. Established in the 1930s under British rule, it has since grown into one of India's major ports, now handling containers, petroleum, and general cargo alongside its traditional bulk trade. The city, nicknamed 'The City of Destiny,' also hosts the headquarters of the Indian Navy's Eastern Naval Command, making it a hub of both commercial and strategic maritime importance.

questions.question: BHEL (Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited) Trichy is a major manufacturing unit for which sector's equipment?
BHEL is classified by the Indian government under which category of public sector enterprise?
In which decade was the BHEL Trichy unit, known as High Pressure Boiler Plant, established?
BHEL Trichy's boilers are primarily supplied to which type of power stations?
BHEL as a company was originally established in which decade with Soviet and Czech technical collaboration?

pins.summary: BHEL's High Pressure Boiler Plant in Tiruchirappalli (Trichy), established in the mid-1960s, is one of the flagship manufacturing units of Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited, India's largest power-sector public enterprise. It manufactures boilers, heat exchangers, and pressure vessels for thermal power stations across India and abroad, playing a central role in the country's power-generation capacity buildup since independence. BHEL itself was founded with early technical collaboration from the Soviet Union and Czechoslovakia and today holds Maharatna status, India's highest tier for public sector companies.

questions.question: Namma Metro is the rapid transit metro system serving which Indian city?
'Namma Metro' translates roughly to what in Kannada?
Namma Metro's first line became operational in which year?
Namma Metro's two original main lines are colour-coded as which pair?
Bengaluru's metro system was built primarily to address which major urban problem?

pins.summary: Namma Metro ('Our Metro' in Kannada) is Bengaluru's rapid transit rail system, launched in 2011 to tackle the city's notoriously severe traffic congestion, born of its rapid growth as India's tech hub. Its original Purple and Green lines have since been extended repeatedly, with several newer lines and extensions under active construction to keep pace with the city's sprawl. Namma Metro is operated by the Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited and has become an essential, if still-expanding, backbone for the city's daily commuters navigating one of India's most gridlocked urban road networks.

questions.question: VSSC is ISRO's lead centre for developing what?
VSSC is named after which figure, considered the father of India's space programme?
VSSC was established at Thumba, near Thiruvananthapuram, in which decade?
The original rocket launching station at Thumba famously used which local building, repurposed for early operations?
VSSC contributed to the development of which major Indian launch vehicle family?

pins.summary: The Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre at Thumba, near Thiruvananthapuram, is ISRO's principal centre for designing and developing India's launch vehicles, including the workhorse PSLV and the heavier GSLV rockets. Named after Vikram Sarabhai, widely regarded as the founder of India's space programme, the site was chosen in the 1960s for its proximity to the geomagnetic equator, ideal for early sounding rocket experiments. In a now-famous detail of India's space history, the fledgling programme's first office and rocket-assembly space were housed in a converted church and bishop's house, since the government initially had no dedicated facilities to offer.

questions.question: Baisakhi, widely celebrated in Punjab, marks both a harvest festival and which significant Sikh historical event?
options: The formation of the Khalsa Panth in 1699
The construction of the Golden Temple

questions.question: Baisakhi typically falls in which month of the year?
Baisakhi also marks the traditional harvest of which major crop in Punjab?
The 1699 Baisakhi gathering where the Khalsa was formed took place at which location?
The energetic harvest folk dance closely associated with Baisakhi celebrations in Punjab is called what?

pins.summary: Baisakhi is one of Punjab's most significant festivals, layering a joyous wheat-harvest celebration over a pivotal moment in Sikh history: in 1699, Guru Gobind Singh formally established the Khalsa Panth at Anandpur Sahib on this day, initiating the first five Sikhs (the Panj Pyare) into a distinct martial and spiritual order. Falling in mid-April, Baisakhi sees fields of golden wheat ready for harvest, farmers offering thanks, and communities coming together for energetic Bhangra performances, processions (nagar kirtans), and langar feasts at gurdwaras across Punjab and the Sikh diaspora worldwide.

questions.question: Losar is the traditional New Year festival of which Himalayan communities?
Losar is typically celebrated in which season?
Losar celebrations traditionally include rituals to drive away what, symbolically, from the old year?
Losar festivities commonly include performances of which traditional masked dance?
Ladakh's Losar is observed roughly two months earlier than the Tibetan Losar in some traditions, largely due to what?

pins.summary: Losar, the Tibetan Buddhist New Year, is celebrated with particular vibrancy across Ladakh, where monasteries come alive with butter lamps, ritual cham masked dances performed by monks, and family gatherings marking the turn of the lunar year. Ladakh actually observes Losar roughly two months ahead of the mainstream Tibetan calendar, a local variation tracing back to older monastic astrological traditions in the region. The festival blends solemn spiritual rites — driving away the misfortunes of the past year — with genuinely festive elements: feasting, archery contests, and communal singing that light up Leh's freezing winter nights.

questions.question: Chhath Puja is primarily a form of worship dedicated to which celestial body?
Chhath Puja rituals uniquely require devotees to offer prayers standing in what?
options: Water (rivers or ponds), at sunrise and sunset

questions.question: Chhath Puja is most strongly associated with which two Indian states?
The Chhath festival spans how many days of rituals?
Chhath Puja rituals are notable for including offerings to the sun during which two specific times?
options: Both sunrise and sunset (setting and rising sun)

pins.summary: Chhath Puja, observed intensely across Bihar and eastern Uttar Pradesh, is a four-day festival dedicated to the Sun God, Surya, distinguished by its rigorous rituals: devotees fast for extended periods and stand waist-deep in rivers or ponds at both sunset and the following sunrise to offer prayers — a rare instance of worship extended to the 'setting' sun as well as the rising one. Patna's riverside ghats along the Ganga become a sea of devotees during Chhath, with elaborate offerings of fruit, sugarcane, and traditional thekua sweets. The festival has spread wherever Bihari and Purvanchali communities have migrated, from Delhi to Mumbai to cities abroad.

questions.question: Rongali (Bohag) Bihu marks the beginning of what in the Assamese calendar?
options: The Assamese New Year and spring sowing season

questions.question: Bohag Bihu is typically celebrated in which month?
Assam actually celebrates three Bihu festivals across the year, tied to which agricultural cycle stages?
The energetic traditional dance performed during Bihu, especially by young men and women, is called what?
Which of the three Bihu festivals is considered the most significant and joyous, marking the new year?

pins.summary: Rongali or Bohag Bihu, celebrated in mid-April, marks the Assamese New Year and the start of the sowing season, making it the most joyous of Assam's three annual Bihu festivals (the others being the more solemn Kati and Magh Bihu, tied to different points in the farming calendar). The festival is inseparable from the vibrant Bihu dance — fast-paced, hip-swaying movements performed by young men and women in traditional Assamese attire, accompanied by the dhol and pepa (buffalo-horn pipe). Bohag Bihu is as much a community and courtship ritual as an agricultural one, historically serving as an occasion for young Assamese to meet and socialise.

questions.question: Teej is a monsoon festival in Rajasthan primarily celebrated by whom?
options: Women, honouring marital bonds and Goddess Parvati

questions.question: Teej festivities in Jaipur famously include a grand procession featuring what?
options: A decorated idol of Goddess Teej Mata carried on a palanquin

questions.question: Teej celebrations commonly involve women wearing which colour prominently?
A traditional activity strongly associated with Teej, especially for young women, is riding what?
Teej is dedicated to the union of Lord Shiva and which goddess?

pins.summary: Teej, arriving with the monsoon rains, is one of Rajasthan's most visually spectacular festivals, dedicated to the union of Shiva and Parvati and celebrated predominantly by women, who dress in vivid green attire symbolising the season's fresh growth, apply intricate mehndi, and swing on flower-decorated jhulas hung from trees. Jaipur hosts the festival's grandest public celebration: a resplendent procession carrying the idol of Teej Mata through the old city on a gold-and-silver palanquin, accompanied by elephants, dancers, and folk musicians, drawing crowds that rival the city's more famous Gangaur festival.

questions.question: Jammu and Kashmir was reorganised from a state into a Union Territory in which year?
The reorganisation of Jammu and Kashmir followed the abrogation of which constitutional article?
Jammu and Kashmir, unlike most other Union Territories, uniquely retains what?
Srinagar serves as which type of capital for Jammu and Kashmir?
options: Summer capital (Jammu is the winter capital)

questions.question: Ladakh was carved out as a separate Union Territory at the same time as the J&K reorganisation. Does Ladakh have its own legislature?
options: No, it is governed without a legislature
Yes, but only for local matters

pins.summary: Jammu and Kashmir was reorganised from a state into a Union Territory in August 2019, following Parliament's abrogation of Article 370, which had granted the former state special autonomous status. Unusually among Union Territories, J&K retains its own Legislative Assembly, giving it a degree of self-governance closer to statehood than most UTs enjoy. The region follows a historic dual-capital system, with Srinagar serving as the summer capital and Jammu as the winter capital, a practice dating back to the era of the Dogra monarchy. Ladakh, split off in the same reorganisation, became a separate UT without its own legislature.

questions.question: Ladakh became a separate Union Territory in which year?
Ladakh is administered directly by which authority, given it has no state legislature?
options: The Governor of Jammu and Kashmir
A Lieutenant Governor appointed by the Centre

questions.question: Ladakh comprises which two main districts?
Ladakh is bordered by which two countries, making it strategically significant?
Local governance in Ladakh's districts is significantly handled by which elected bodies?

pins.summary: Ladakh became India's newest Union Territory in October 2019, split from the former state of Jammu and Kashmir, and is administered by a Lieutenant Governor rather than an elected legislature, since Parliament did not grant it a state assembly. Local governance instead runs significantly through the Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils for Leh and Kargil districts, which handle many day-to-day administrative matters. Bordering both China and Pakistan, Ladakh occupies a strategically sensitive position in India's north, and its cold desert landscape, Buddhist monastic culture, and remoteness have made it an increasingly popular high-altitude tourism destination even as it remains a militarily significant frontier region.

location.name: Port Blair — Andaman and Nicobar Islands

questions.question: Port Blair is the capital of which Union Territory?
The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are located in which body of water?
Port Blair was historically infamous for housing which colonial-era prison?
The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are administered by which official appointed by the Centre?
The Nicobar group, distinct from the Andamans, is home to several tribes, including the isolated inhabitants of which island?

pins.summary: Port Blair, capital of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands Union Territory, sits in the Bay of Bengal roughly 1,300 km from the Indian mainland, making this one of India's most geographically remote administrative capitals. The city is historically notorious for the Cellular Jail, or 'Kala Pani,' where the British imprisoned Indian freedom fighters in near-total isolation. Administered by a Centrally appointed Lieutenant Governor, the territory includes the Nicobar group further south, home to the reclusive Sentinelese people of North Sentinel Island, among the last uncontacted tribes on Earth, protected by strict government-enforced isolation.

questions.question: Telangana became India's newest state (before Ladakh's UT status) by bifurcation from which state in 2014?
Telangana officially came into existence on which date in 2014?
Hyderabad serves an unusual dual role as the capital of which two entities for a transitional period?
options: Only Telangana, no dual role existed

questions.question: The demand for a separate Telangana state was rooted in grievances over what, among Telangana-region residents?
options: Perceived regional neglect and unequal development
Border conflicts with a neighbouring country

questions.question: The movement for Telangana statehood was politically spearheaded prominently by which party?

pins.summary: Telangana was carved out of Andhra Pradesh on 2 June 2014, becoming India's 29th state after a decades-long movement rooted in claims of regional neglect and unequal development for the Telangana region compared to coastal Andhra. The Telangana Rashtra Samithi, founded specifically to press this demand, spearheaded the political campaign that eventually led Parliament to pass the bifurcation bill. Hyderabad, the shared former capital, served as the joint capital of both Telangana and residual Andhra Pradesh for a transitional ten-year period, an unusual arrangement designed to give Andhra Pradesh time to develop a new capital, which it later began building at Amaravati.

questions.question: Uttarakhand was carved out of which larger state in 2000?
Uttarakhand was originally named what, before being officially renamed in 2007?
Dehradun serves as which type of capital for Uttarakhand?
options: Interim/current capital (Gairsain proposed as summer capital)

questions.question: The demand for a separate hill state that became Uttarakhand grew significantly during a mass movement in which decade?
Uttarakhand's two main historical-cultural regions are Garhwal and which other?

pins.summary: Uttarakhand was carved out of Uttar Pradesh in November 2000, becoming India's 27th state after a sustained hill-state movement through the 1990s that argued the Himalayan districts had distinct geographic, cultural, and developmental needs poorly served by governance from the plains. Initially named Uttaranchal, it was officially renamed Uttarakhand in 2007, restoring what many residents felt was its more historically resonant name. Dehradun serves as the current seat of government, though Gairsain, more centrally located in the hills, has been designated a proposed summer capital — part of a long-running debate over whether the state's administration should sit closer to its mountainous heartland.
